acceptance: 1) Caller/wiring point: real POST messages -> cookie-scope/OPEN checks -> row-locked seq/message/outbox/90-day deadline in one transaction. Same clientMessageId/payload returns the original id/seq with one notification; changed payload returns 409. closed/anonymized rejects; failed writes change nothing (E-18, E-33, E-90). 2) Drop the HTTP response after successful persistence, then retry the original UUID/payload and receive the same receipt. Only the initial commit advances 90 days; reads/notifications do not. Expired/revoked credentials or another person's id/email cannot read or write (E-37, E-78, E-86).

E-18.trigger: The same message is submitted repeatedly because of retries.
E-18.expect: Deduplicate by the client message identifier so the inbox contains one message and notifications are not triggered repeatedly.

E-33.scene: C-01 Human inbox and reply entry points
E-33.trigger: Two authorized people reply concurrently, or a visitor repeats the same client message identifier.
E-33.expect: Order by server seq and show the actual author. The same clientMessageId and payload in the same conversation produce only one message, one outbox item, and one unread increment. Persist each concurrent human reply; a later response must not overwrite an earlier saved reply.

E-37.scene: C-02 Offline messages and recovery from send failures
E-37.trigger: Submission times out or the response is lost, leaving actual persistence unknown.
E-37.expect: Show a confirmation-pending or retryable state. Retry with the original client message identifier and return the original receipt result, without duplicating inbox or notification items.

E-78.trigger: A visitor session expires or is revoked, or an operator loses chat permission after previously holding ADMIN/SALES.
E-78.expect: Perform server-side authorization on the next poll and send, and stop returning conversation content. Changing threadId, seq, or email cannot read another consultation.

E-86.trigger: A hidden tab still polls, or a visit merely refreshes without successfully sending or receiving a consultation message.
E-86.expect: These behaviors do not postpone the 90-day retention deadline for messages/email. Consultation activity means successfully persisted visitor messages or human replies; notification retries, delivery receipts, and read-state updates do not count as new consultation activity.

E-90.trigger: The process stops immediately after saving a message, or a client resends the same message following a timeout.
E-90.expect: Save the message and an outbox record unique by messageId in the same database transaction. Notifications for committed messages can continue after restart; a message-idempotency hit cannot create a second notification.
